content: 1. Physical violence refers to any act that causes physical harm or injury to another person through the use of force. 2. Sexual violence involves any non-consensual sexual act or behavior, including coercion or physical force. 3. Threats of physical or sexual violence include verbal or non-verbal actions that instill fear of harm or assault. 4. Psychological or emotional abuse encompasses behaviors that harm an individual’s mental health or emotional well-being, such as manipulation, intimidation, or verbal aggression. It can also result from the absence of essential elements like oxygen or heat. Disability Disability refers to any impairment that restricts or prevents an individual from performing actions or activities in a manner or range considered normal. Medical Health Care Medical health care involves treatment provided by a physician or other healthcare professional to address the physical health needs of the victim. Mental Health Care Mental health care includes individual or group therapy provided by psychiatrists, psychologists, social workers, or counselors to address the mental health needs of the victim. This care may be delivered in inpatient or outpatient settings. It excludes substance abuse treatment and pastoral counseling unless specifically related to the victim’s mental health. Substance Abuse Treatment Substance abuse treatment focuses on addressing issues related to the victim’s use of alcohol or other drugs. To protect victim privacy and confidentiality, access to this data must be restricted to authorized personnel. Case Identification A unique case identifier may be assigned by the agency compiling IPV (intimate partner violence) surveillance data or by the contributing data source. This identifier may or may not be identical to the one used for linking data across multiple sources. Data Standards and Guidelines The data type for identifiers is an extended composite ID with a check digit. Components include the primary identifier, check digit, and code indicating the check digit scheme. Additional components are used only for local purposes if needed. Relational Databases for Surveillance Surveillance systems often require combining data from multiple sources, such as healthcare and police records, using relational databases. This allows for comprehensive data collection across various elements. A unique identifier is necessary to link data across all sources. Documentation of IPV Victimization The date of IPV victimization documentation reflects when the agency first recorded the incident. If no prior documentation exists, this date may coincide with the most recent violent episode. Race of Victim Data on the race of victims is used in public health surveillance, epidemiologic research, and health services studies. Federal standards promote uniformity in race and ethnicity data collection to monitor equal access and address historical discrimination. Racial categories are social-political constructs and are not scientifically precise or mutually exclusive. Self-identification is preferred for determining race, and individuals of mixed racial origins should be coded using multiple categories rather than a single multiracial category.
